subject: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@acme-retail.com>, Tom Green <tgreen@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: POC follow-up: next steps & proposed eval plan

Hi Sofia / Tom —

Great to speak with you today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call: 

- Goal: Validate model performance on multilingual customer support (EN/ES) and retrieval-augmented responses for product lookup.
- Success criteria (proposal):
  1) Answer accuracy: >= 85% of sampled tickets match human label on intent + entity extraction.
  2) Latency: 95th percentile < 350ms for single-turn query on dedicated instance.
  3) Cost target: average token cost <= $0.0025 per request under expected load.
  4) Multilingual F1 (EN/ES) >= 0.80 for intent classification.

Proposed evaluation plan: attached is a draft POC evaluation spreadsheet (acme_poc_eval_plan.xlsx) with sample prompts, labeling rubric, and timeline. High level: 2-week trial, week 1 smoke + integration, week 2 focused evaluation with ~500 sample queries per language.

Model selection for trial: based on the use-case (multilingual QA + retrieval), we recommend:
- Primary model: mT5-large quantized variant (good multilingual base + strong seq2seq for QA).
- Fallback model: Llama 2 13B (4-bit quantized) tuned for instruction-following as a lower-latency, cost-efficient fallback for non-sensitive queries.

We’ll set up two endpoints: primary (mT5-large, retrieval enabled) and fallback (Llama 2 13B, cached responses). Routing policy: prefer primary; fallback on latency or rate limit breaches.

Ownership / next steps:
- Redwood (Ben): provision trial endpoints, share test credentials, and fill in model profiles (ETA 2 business days).
- Acme (Sofia): provide sample dataset (minimum 500 queries, EN+ES) and define top-10 success intents (ETA 3 business days).
- Joint: schedule a kickoff integration call (30m) — propose Monday Mar 1, 10am PT.

Attachments: acme_poc_eval_plan.xlsx, model-profiles.pdf

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Tom Green <tgreen@acme-retail.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 27 Feb 2026 08:21:00 -0800
Subject: Re: POC follow-up: next steps & proposed eval plan

Hi Sofia — thanks for the quick reply and great questions. Answers inline below.

> 1) Dataset format
Yes, CSV with columns (id, text, language, priority, expected_response [optional]) works well. If you can flag examples that require retrieval (product-specific answers), add a boolean column `requires_kg`.

> 2) Latency / infra
We plan to run the trial on a dedicated NVidia A10x4 pool with Redwood Dedicated. In our benchmarks that setup achieves ~280ms p95 for mT5-large with retrieval disabled. With retrieval enabled and a small local FAISS index (recommended for this POC), we expect ~300-350ms p95 depending on average context length. We'll instrument tracing so you can see request breakdown. If the p95 slips we'll add autoscale burst capacity or route to the faster quantized fallback for tail requests.

> 3) Fallback model tradeoffs
Llama 2 13B (4-bit quant) is a tradeoff: generally lower latency and cost vs mT5-large for short instruction-following queries, but its multilingual QA is not as strong as mT5. We chose it as a fallback for throughput-sensitive paths and to keep costs manageable if traffic spikes. Alternative is a smaller mT5 (eg. mT5-base) as fallback — if you want stronger multilingual parity at slightly higher cost, we can do that.

Next steps:
- Ben: finalize endpoints + share test keys by Mon Feb 29 (we'll provision earlier if dataset arrives).
- Acme (Sofia): drop CSV to the Drive link and ping when ready.
- Marissa (Redwood Solutions): will coordinate ingestion and evaluation scripts.

I'll add Marissa and Laura to own technical onboarding. See you Monday.

Best,
Ben

Adding a quick implementation runbook for the kickoff: 

- Day 0 (kickoff call): confirm dataset format, share Drive link, confirm sample intents, and finalize routing rules (primary vs fallback).
- Day 1: Redwood provisions endpoints (mT5-large primary, Llama2-13B fallback), provide API keys + example curl.
- Day 2-3: Ingestion & smoke tests — we’ll run 50 sample queries per language and validate basic correctness & latency.
- Day 4-7: Full evaluation run — run ~500 queries per language, collect model outputs, and push to labeling queue (we'll provide a simple UI).
- Day 8-10: Analysis & tuning — compare metrics vs success criteria, tune prompt templates, and test rerouting thresholds.

Ownership:
- Redwood: Marissa (technical lead) and Ben (commercial lead)
- Acme: Sofia (project lead) and Tom (data lead)

Deliverables: evaluation report (PDF), raw output CSV, and a short recommendation (model + routing) at the end of the trial.

Attachments referenced: acme_poc_eval_plan.xlsx (drive link in Ben's email).

Marissa Cole
